state.spending_context: Independent spending, not campaign contributions or proof of candidate policy. Organization context explains documented relevance; unmapped spenders have unestablished relevance and should not explain a Palestine assessment without other explicit evidence. Top 12 per direction plus all registered relevant spenders; not exhaustive totals. Funding links do not establish earmarking, control, or that every ad concerns Israel/Palestine.
campaign_platform_points: Housing: Opposes exclusionary zoning, supports building 100,000 new units in San Francisco over 10 years, statewide minimum density near transit, a $10 billion housing bond, expanding rent control, overturning Costa Hawkins, and extending eviction protections for tenants.

Homelessness: Supports a range of interventions including supportive housing, mental health care, addiction treatment, rapid rehousing vouchers, purchasing hotels for immediate housing, and a billionaire wealth tax to fund navigation centers and wrap-around services.

Economy & cost of living: Proposes a state-level executive pay tax targeting companies where top executives earn over 100 times median worker pay, tuition-free college, universal healthcare, expanding guaranteed income to end child poverty within five years, and protecting labor rights including for gig workers.

Environment & climate: Supports a California Green New Deal focused on environmental justice for low-income and immigrant communities, green infrastructure investment, completing high-speed rail, reforming environmental review to unblock clean energy projects, and wildfire and drought preparedness.

Criminal justice & public safety: Advocates community policing with diverse recruitment, criminal justice reform emphasizing rehabilitation and treatment over incarceration, stopping organized crime fueling the fentanyl epidemic and retail theft, and a state fund for individuals and businesses affected by hate crimes.

Civil liberties, privacy & surveillance: Supports dismantling systemic racism in California institutions, paid family leave, universal childcare, police accountability for civil rights violations, and protecting voting rights, LGBTQ+ rights, immigrant rights, and reproductive rights for all Californians.
Homelessness: The campaign states that housing more homeless people is a core priority, with Matt Haney committing to champion solutions on homelessness for all San Franciscans at the state level.
Housing: The campaign's stated platform explicitly focuses on addressing the housing crisis as one of its central issues, alongside homelessness, climate change, and inequality.

antisemitism_education_policy_evidence.summary: CalMatters lists Matt Haney as recorded Aye on AB 715 (Assembly Floor). The bill creates an antisemitism coordinator and classroom-material oversight; its text does not explicitly name IHRA.
antisemitism_education_policy_evidence.context: Tracker date, not an independently verified official roll call.

caste_legislation_context.weight: LOW WEIGHT context, not a Gaza position. The 2023 California SB 403 caste-discrimination bill (vetoed by Newsom; the 2025 SB 403 is an unrelated bill) concerns Hindutva accountability — a parallel the owner values against supremacist ideologies, but it ranks far below Gaza. This context may shift the score at most 0.2 in either direction and must NEVER move a grade band on its own: authoring or voting aye is small positive; demanding removal of the word "caste", co-signing a delay-and-study letter, or abstaining is small negative. Grade strictly on the Gaza record; mention caste history only when actually relevant to this candidate.

items.summary: Haney voted aye on SB 403 (caste bill) in Assembly Judiciary and on final Assembly passage 2023-08-28, retaining the word caste.
items.context: Tracker date, not an independently verified official roll call.

gaza_evidence: 2026-02-23: Haney invited HEAL Palestine's Global Healing children from Gaza to the California State Assembly floor in Sacramento to speak about their treatment.

2026-10-23: Haney publicly called Israel’s actions in Gaza a genocide in CAIR-SFBA’s 2026 Liberty Award recording. The owner confirmed this statement in the linked video. Date context: Date is the official CAIRSFBA video upload date, not a verified speech date. Statement content is owner-confirmed; a transcript and exact timestamp were not independently retrievable.
state.funding_scope: Organization funding since 2024 only; unresolved or mixed totals omitted, not proof of zero funding.
state.endorsement_evidence_context: For this rubric, directional CAIR Action / Vote for Peace recommendations, including Ally or Opposed, are concrete stance evidence even without a direct candidate quotation. Preserve their stated tier, phase and source qualifications.

California Jewish Democrats.relevance: California Jewish Democrats is the renamed Democrats for Israel California (same organization; dfi-ca.org).

CAIR Action.relevance: Recommendations consider civil rights and foreign policy, including Gaza/ceasefire positions. Preferred is not full endorsement; preserve the recorded tier and joint status.

Vote for Peace.relevance: Evaluates human rights and war-lobby/AIPAC funding, also considering viability. Preserve Ally/Neutral/Opposed; inclusion alone is not endorsement or proof of a specific policy.
